newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt reaches broad budget accord - Greens.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt reaches broad budget accord - Greens.

text.p: Coalition parties supporting the Italian government, including Communist Refoundation, have reached a broad accord on the mini-budget, the parliamentary leader of the Green party said.

Speaking as he left a meeting of coalition party leaders, Maurizio Pieroni told reporters the centre-left government had been given the green light to approve the budget at a cabinet meeting on Thursday.
"There has been a broad agreement," Pieroni said. "The government has the proxy to do everything tomorrow," he added.
A cabinet meeting has been called for 0830 GMT on Thursday.
The leader of the Popular Party, Franco Marini, also confirmed that there had been a broad consensus on the government proposals, but added that some fine tuning still needed to be done.
The mini-budget is expected to include up to 16 trillion lire of deficit cutting measures in a bid to prepare the economy for the launch of the single European currency.
"The overhaul of the public debt is something we have to do for future generations," Pieroni said.
"The problem is that up until now the same (people) have always had to pay. There was a broad accord on the redistribution of the costs of the overhaul."
He did not go into further details.
The mini-budget is expected to include the transfer of between 6.0 to 7.0 trillion lire of company severance payment funds into Treasury coffers.
Italian industrialists use the funds as a cheap source of self-financing and have warned that such a measure would harm businesses. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
